title: Zscaler Support access to Cloud & Branch Connector: Admin Console remote assistance and the zssupport tunnel into connector VMs

prose.text: Zscaler Support can reach a Cloud & Branch Connector deployment in two separate ways: through the Admin Console, and through the connector VM. {{console-remote-assistance}} {{vm-remote-access}}

prose.label: Admin Console remote assistance.
prose.text: {{durations}} {{obfuscate}} Who may change the setting is a role permission: [[shared.admin-rbac.cloud-connector:remote-assistance-perm]].

prose.label: Open.
prose.text: What Obfuscate Data hides, the longest allowed duration and the host the zssupport tunnel connects to are not given {{gap:remote-assistance-details}}.

checks.do: For a support tunnel that will not start, that outbound SSH on port 12002 is allowed, that every command was run with sudo, and the ecsupport log for the failure.
For Support that cannot log in to the VM, that the support tunnel was explicitly enabled, since the feature is disabled by default.
For Support that cannot reach the Admin Console, whether the Remote Assistance window is still open and the access level selected.

console-remote-assistance.statement: Remote assistance lets Zscaler Support log in to the portal with either view-only or full admin privileges until the specified date; it is set at Help > Tools & Resources > Remote Assistance by selecting Allow Remote Assistance, then View Only, Full Access (Read/Write), or both.

quotes: Remote assistance allows Zscaler Support to securely and remotely log in to the portal. This can be done with either view-only or full admin privileges.
This procedure allows Zscaler Support to access the portal until the specified date.
Select Allow Remote Assistance, then select View Only, Full Access (Read/Write), or both.
Go to Help > Tools & Resources > Remote Assistance.

durations.statement: Zscaler recommends a length of at least one year when choosing view-only access and at least two days when choosing full access.

quotes: Zscaler recommends that you select a length of at least one year when choosing view-only access and at least two days when choosing full access.

obfuscate.statement: Obfuscate Data is off by default, and admins with Remote Assistance Management enabled for their role can make changes in the Remote Assistance window.

quotes: Select Obfuscate Data if desired. By default, this is set to off.
Admins with Remote Assistance Management enabled for their role can make changes in the Remote Assistance window.

vm-remote-access.statement: An admin can request remote access and allow Zscaler Support to log in to their Cloud or Branch Connector VM instance without opening a firewall connection for inbound traffic; the feature is disabled by default and must be explicitly enabled for the duration of the support assistance.

quotes: An admin can request remote access and allow Zscaler Support to log in to their Zscaler Cloud or Branch Connector virtual machine (VM) instance without opening a firewall connection for inbound traffic.
This feature is disabled by default. You must explicitly enable it for the duration that you need remote support assistance.

zssupport-commands.statement: The zssupport tunnel has a command that creates a long-lived SSH tunnel to the Zscaler cloud with remote port forwarding, which needs outbound SSH traffic allowed on port 12002 because the support servers monitor through this port; another brings the tunnel and all remote connections down, a third checks its status, and every command must include sudo.

quotes: This command creates a long-lived SSH tunnel to the Zscaler cloud and sets up remote port forwarding, which allows Zscaler Support to log in to your Cloud or Branch Connector instance.
To run this command, allow outbound SSH traffic on port 12002 because the support servers monitor through this port.
This command brings down the long-lived SSH tunnel to the Zscaler cloud and all the remote connections.
This command checks the status of the long-lived SSH tunnel to the Zscaler cloud, which Zscaler Support uses to log in to your Cloud or Branch Connector instance.
Ensure that you include sudo in every command that you run.

evidence.after: - To enable Zscaler Support to access your Cloud or Branch Connector instance:
quotes: sudo zssupport tunnel start

evidence.after: - To disable Zscaler Support access to your Cloud or Branch Connector instance:
quotes: sudo zssupport tunnel stop

evidence.after: - To check the status of the Zscaler Support access to your Cloud or Branch Connector instance:
quotes: sudo zssupport tunnel status

ssm-path.statement: If the admin is using AWS Session Manager, the path environment variable is exported (including /home/zsroot/bin) before running sudo zssupport tunnel start.

quotes: If you are using Amazon Web Service (AWS) Session Manager (SSM), export the path environment variable and then run the command:
export PATH=/sbin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/home/zsroot/bin sudo zssupport tunnel start

support-log.statement: If the support tunnel enablement fails, the logs at /var/log/zscaler/ecsupport/ecsupport.log are to be attached for debugging.

quotes: If the support tunnel enablement fails, attach the logs at /var/log/zscaler/ecsupport/ecsupport.log for debugging.

firewall-url.statement: The firewall requirements are at https://config.zscaler.com/<Zscaler Cloud Name>/cloud-branch-connector, where the cloud name is the one in the URL used to log in to the Admin Console.

quotes: To view your firewall requirements, go to the following URL: https://config.zscaler.com/<Zscaler Cloud Name>/cloud-branch-connector.
You can find the <Zscaler Cloud Name> in the URL you use to log in to the Zscaler Admin Console.

remote-assistance-details.title: What Obfuscate Data hides, the longest remote assistance duration and the zssupport tunnel host
remote-assistance-details.detail: The remote assistance page does not say what Obfuscate Data hides or the longest duration allowed, and the remote access page does not name the host the tunnel connects to; cloud-connector.aws.security-groups has remotesupport.<cloud>.net from the Terraform module and the CloudFormation templates (cfn-support-ip).
